hurricane.gloss: a severe tropical cyclone usually with heavy rains and winds moving at 63-136 knots (12 on the Beaufort scale)

hurried.gloss: moving rapidly or performed quickly or in great haste
hurried.example: a hurried trip to the store

hurry.gloss: a condition of urgency making it necessary to hurry
hurry.example: in a hurry to lock the door
The runner zipped past us at breakneck pace

hurt.gloss: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
any physical damage to the body caused by violence or accident or fracture etc.; the condition of an injury

hurting.gloss: a symptom of some physical hurt or disorder
hurting.example: the patient developed severe pain and distension

husband.gloss: a married man; a woman's partner in marriage

husband.example: I try to economize my spare time

husky.gloss: breed of heavy-coated Arctic sled dog
deep and harsh sounding as if from shouting or illness or emotion

hussite.gloss: an adherent of the religious reforms of John Huss

hut.gloss: small crude shelter used as a dwelling

hutu.gloss: a member of a Bantu people living in Rwanda and Burundi

hybrid.gloss: a word that is composed of parts from different languages (e.g., ‘monolingual’ has a Greek prefix and a Latin root)

hybrid.example: the vice-presidency is a hybrid of administrative and legislative offices

hybridization.gloss: (genetics) the act of mixing different species or varieties of animals or plants and thus to produce hybrids

hydra.gloss: (Greek mythology) monster with nine heads; when struck off each head was replaced by two new ones
trouble that cannot be overcome by a single effort because of its many aspects or its persistent and pervasive quality
hydra.example: we may be facing a hydra that defies any easy solution

hydra.gloss: small tubular solitary freshwater hydrozoan polyp

hydrate.gloss: any compound that contains water of crystallization
supply water or liquid to in order to maintain a healthy balance
hydrate.example: the bicyclists must be hydrated frequently

hydrate.gloss: become hydrated and combine with water

hydrated.gloss: containing combined water (especially water of crystallization as in a hydrate)

hydration.gloss: the process of combining with water; usually reversible

hydraulic.gloss: moved or operated or effected by liquid (water or oil)
of or relating to the study of hydraulics

hydraulics.gloss: study of the mechanics of fluids

hydrazine.gloss: a colorless fuming corrosive liquid; a powerful reducing agent; used chiefly in rocket fuels

hydrocarbon.gloss: an organic compound containing only carbon and hydrogen

hydroelectric.gloss: of or relating to or used in the production of electricity by waterpower

hydrogen.gloss: a nonmetallic univalent element that is normally a colorless and odorless highly flammable diatomic gas; the simplest and lightest and most abundant element in the universe

hydrographic.gloss: of or relating to the science of hydrography

hydrography.gloss: the science of the measurement and description and mapping of the surface waters of the earth with special reference to navigation

hydrology.gloss: the branch of geology that studies water on the earth and in the atmosphere: its distribution and uses and conservation

hydrolysis.gloss: a chemical reaction in which water reacts with a compound to produce other compounds; involves the splitting of a bond and the addition of the hydrogen cation and the hydroxide anion from the water

hydrolyze.gloss: undergo hydrolysis; decompose by reacting with water

hydrophilic.gloss: having a strong affinity for water; tending to dissolve in, mix with, or be wetted by water

hydrophobic.gloss: lacking affinity for water; tending to repel and not absorb water; tending not to dissolve in or mix with or be wetted by water

hydrosphere.gloss: the watery layer of the earth's surface; includes water vapor

hydrostatic.gloss: relating to fluids at rest or to the pressures they exert or transmit

hydroxide.gloss: a compound of an oxide with water
a chemical compound containing the hydroxyl group

hyena.gloss: doglike nocturnal mammal of Africa and southern Asia that feeds chiefly on carrion

hygiene.gloss: the science concerned with the prevention of illness and maintenance of health

hymn.gloss: a song of praise (to God or to a saint or to a nation)

hymn.example: They hymned their love of God

hypertension.gloss: a common disorder in which blood pressure remains abnormally high (a reading of 140/90 mm Hg or greater)

hypertext.gloss: machine-readable text that is not sequential but is organized so that related items of information are connected
hypertext.example: Let me introduce the word hypertext to mean a body of written or pictorial material interconnected in such a complex way that it could not conveniently be presented or represented on paper

hypertrophy.gloss: abnormal enlargement of a body part or organ

hypertrophy.example: muscles can hypertrophy when people take steroids

hypocrisy.gloss: an expression of agreement that is not supported by real conviction
insincerity by virtue of pretending to have qualities or beliefs that you do not really have

hypoglycemia.gloss: abnormally low blood sugar usually resulting from excessive insulin or a poor diet

hypothesis.gloss: a proposal intended to explain certain facts or observations
a tentative insight into the natural world; a concept that is not yet verified but that if true would explain certain facts or phenomena
hypothesis.example: a scientific hypothesis that survives experimental testing becomes a scientific theory

hypothesis.gloss: a message expressing an opinion based on incomplete evidence

hysteria.gloss: neurotic disorder characterized by violent emotional outbreaks and disturbances of sensory and motor functions

hz.gloss: the unit of frequency; one hertz has a periodic interval of one second (named for Heinrich Rudolph Hertz)
